title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go, parity fixes, v1.90.0
author: Maya Chen
description: Unify authentication, retry semantics and streaming ergonomics across Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs; apply parity fixes and bump SDK versions to v1.90.0. Motivation: multiple downstream teams reported subtle differences between SDKs in how auth refreshes, retry backoff and streaming reconnects were handled which led to production discrepancies (ENG-9123). This PR consolidates behavior into a single canonical design and implements it across the three SDKs along with small API ergonomics improvements and coordinated version bumps. Summary of changes: - Introduced unified auth provider interface and refresh flow (token refresh is now explicit, pluggable and consistent across SDKs). - Standardized retry policy (idempotency-aware default, exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts configurable). - Streaming ergonomics: stable reconnect helper, backpressure-aware client-side buffering, deterministic stream close semantics and consistent event names across SDKs. - Parity fixes: align field names and error codes returned by SDKs to match server contract; fix a bug in TS streaming where aborted streams could leak sockets. - Version bumps and changelog entries for python v1.90.0, typescript v1.90.0, go v1.90.0. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear tasks linked (ENG-9123, ENG-9234) - [x] Unit and integration tests added for core flows - [x] E2E smoke tests for streaming reconnects - [x] Updated changelogs and release notes - [x] Coordinated release PRs for each SDK Breaking changes: none for typical users; advanced users overriding internal retry hooks may need to adjust to the new interface (migration notes below). Migration notes: - Python: AuthProvider now requires refresh_token() callback signature (see examples in docs). Small adapter included for the old pattern that will log a deprecation warning for one release. - TypeScript: RetryPolicy options moved under clientOptions.retry; old alias is still accepted but deprecated. - Go: New StreamingReconnect helper exposed in streamutil package; existing consumers can opt-in. Impact: reduces cross-language bugs, simplifies long-running streaming jobs, and reduces auth-related 401s seen during refresh windows. Links: design doc: linear/ENG-9123, incident notes: SUP-4521, related infra PRs: redwood/redwood#6021
